feedback.Physical Object: Excluded — A calendar system is abstract; it is not a tangible object.
feedback.Synthetic: Included — All calendars are human-constructed symbolic systems.
feedback.Biological/Biomimetic: Excluded — While inspired by celestial rhythms, calendars are not biomimetic.
feedback.Powered: Excluded — It is inert as a system; does not consume or require power.
feedback.Structural: Excluded — Has no architectural or load-bearing function.
feedback.Observable: Excluded — Only representations of calendars are visible.
feedback.Physical Medium: Excluded — Exists as an abstract rule system.
feedback.Active: Excluded — Requires external systems to be instantiated or applied.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Excluded — A calendar is an evolved conceptual standard, not a discrete functional artifact.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Excluded — It structures expectations but produces no output itself.
feedback.Processes Signals/Logic: Excluded — It defines symbolic relations, not transformations.
feedback.State-Transforming: Excluded — Does not alter internal or external states.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Excluded — Humans consult or use calendars, but the concept itself is passive.
feedback.System-integrated: Excluded — Used by systems, but not embedded functionally.
feedback.Functionally Autonomous: Excluded — Cannot function without human or software instantiation.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — Systems may operate without formal calendars.
feedback.Symbolic: Included — Dates and periods are symbolic representations of time.
feedback.Signalling: Included — Conveys time-related meanings: events, seasons, cycles.
feedback.Rule-governed: Included — Operates via defined conventions (e.g., leap years, months).
feedback.Compositional: Included — Built from nested components (days, weeks, months).
feedback.Normative: Included — Defines when things 'should' happen (e.g., deadlines, holidays).
feedback.Meta: Included — Used to structure and reference other symbolic systems.
feedback.Temporal: Included — Encodes the passage and division of time.
feedback.Digital/Virtual: Included — Exists as a fully abstract structure, often instantiated digitally.
feedback.Social Construct: Included — Requires shared cultural or civil agreement.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Included — Standardized and legislated by governments and institutions.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Excluded — Not inherently tied to personal identity (though calendars can vary culturally).
feedback.Regulated: Included — Official calendars govern public schedules and events.
feedback.Economically Significant: Included — Business, finance, labor, and logistics depend heavily on calendar systems.
feedback.Politicised: Included — Reforms and disputes over calendar systems (e.g., Gregorian vs. Julian) reflect political control.
feedback.Ritualised: Excluded — While it frames rituals, the calendar system itself is not a ritual practice.
feedback.Ethically Significant: Excluded — Calendar rules carry no intrinsic ethical dimension.

encoding_notes: This encoding captures the calendar as a normative, rule-governed, symbolic structure that organizes time socially and economically. It excludes functional traits to reflect its passive, conceptual nature, and emphasizes its temporal, political, and digital abstraction.
